newsitem.title: USA: Security measures at bombing trial back to normal.
newsitem.headline: Security measures at bombing trial back to normal.

text.p: The Oklahoma City bombing trial resumed Friday with normal security measures in place after special precautions were taken the night before, Justice Department sources said.

Prosecutors arrived separately Friday at the courthouse in their normal fashion either with no bodyguards or only one, in contrast to Thursday night when lead prosecutor Joseph Hartzler left surrounded by security agents.
A Justice Department source told Reuters that the security concern, which was never specified, no longer existed.
Speculation arose that security measures were heightened after the FBI conducted a firearms and explosives raid on the Denver-area home of a man who identified himself with the Branch Davidian Cult.

Prosecutors have said that Timothy McVeigh was so outraged by the attack on the cult in Waco, Texas, in 1993 in which leader David Koresh and about 80 followers were killed that he vowed revenge by bombing the Alfred P. Murrah federal building in Oklahoma City exactly two years later.

"I don't know if it (a security concern) ever existed," Hartzler told Reuters when he entered the courthouse Friday with his usual one bodyguard. "I don't know if it exists now. I don't talk about security."
